---
title: viewTransition
description: Enable ViewTransition API from React in App Router
version: experimental
---

`viewTransition` enables React's [View Transitions API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/View_Transition_API) integration in Next.js. This lets you animate navigations, loading states, and content changes using the native browser View Transitions API.

To enable this feature, you need to set the `viewTransition` property to `true` in your `next.config.js` file.

```js filename="next.config.js"
/** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */
const nextConfig = {
  experimental: {
    viewTransition: true,
  },
}

module.exports = nextConfig
```

> [!NOTE]
> The [`<ViewTransition>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/ViewTransition) component is provided by React.
> The `experimental.viewTransition` flag enables Next.js integration, such as triggering
> transitions during route navigations.

## Usage

You can import the [`<ViewTransition>` Component](https://react.dev/reference/react/ViewTransition) from React in your application:

```jsx
import { ViewTransition } from 'react'
```

### Live Demo

Check out the [View Transitions Demo](https://react-view-transitions-demo.labs.vercel.dev) to see this feature in action, or read the [designing view transitions guide](/docs/app/guides/view-transitions) for a step-by-step walkthrough.

The View Transitions API is a baseline web standard, and browser support continues to expand. As React's [`<ViewTransition>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/ViewTransition) component evolves, more transition patterns and use cases will become available.

events.content:
View transitions are wired up across the gallery using React’s `<ViewTransition>` API and Next.js’s experimental integration.

### Configuration
- Enabled `experimental.viewTransition` in `next.config.ts`
- Upgraded `react` / `react-dom` to canary (required for `<ViewTransition>`; stable 19.2 does not export it yet)

### Shared element morph (grid → detail)
Product thumbnails and hero images share a transition name so the browser morphs between them:

```tsx
<ViewTransition name={`product-${product.slug}`} share="morph">
```

### Directional page slides
- Product links use `transitionTypes={['nav-forward']}`
- Back link uses `transitionTypes={['nav-back']}`
- `PageTransition` maps those types to slide animations
- The “Products” heading and back link stay fixed via `view-transition-name`

### Suspense reveals
Both the home grid and product detail info use:
- **Exit:** skeleton slides down (`slide-down`)
- **Enter:** content slides up (`slide-up`) with `default="none"` so it doesn’t fire on unrelated navigations

### Reduced motion
`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` disables all view-transition animations (instant swaps) and stops skeleton pulse animations.

Run `npm run dev` and click between the grid and a product page to see the morph + slide. Browsers without View Transition support still work; transitions are simply skipped.

Both the home grid and product detail info use:
- **Exit:** skeleton slides down (`slide-down`)
- **Enter:** content slides up (`slide-up`) with `default="none"` so it doesn’t fire on unrelated navigations

### Reduced motion
`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` disables all view-transition animations (instant swaps) and stops skeleton pulse animations.

Run `npm run dev` and click between the grid and a product page to see the morph + slide. Browsers without View Transition support still work; transitions are simply skipped.
